newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria to ban gene maize imports from early Jan.
newsitem.headline: Austria to ban gene maize imports from early Jan.

text.p: Austria will ban the import of genetically modified maize manufactured by Swiss Ciba-Geigy AG from early January, the health ministry said on Monday.
"We argued against allowing the import at European Union level. We are concerned about antibiotics and that is why we are introducing the ban," Health Minister Christa Krammer told Austrian radio.
The European Commission approved the sale of gene-modified maize last week, despite Austrian objections.

The engineered maize will be imported from the United States where farmers have planted a type of corn developed by Ciba-Geigy. The maize is resistant to the herbicide glufonisate and the corn-borer pest and carries an antibiotic "marker gene".
Krammer said insufficient work had been done on the effects of the antiobiotic-resistant gene ampicillin. "We have won ourselves some time," she said.
The ban will come into force on January 8 or 9, when the EU Commission decision takes effect. It will initially last three months, pending an investigation by the EU Commission.
